concrete_capability_transition: Headless run completion closure, accepted-completion lookup, and finalization owner selection move from workspace-global task history to the active runtime journey/session graph.

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Allows repeated independent Brownie CLI journeys in one repository to complete and finalize the active journey graph rather than all historical workspace tasks.
Makes runtime progress and completion views reflect the active journey scope instead of unrelated workspace history.
Includes typed descendants, recovery, retry, and continuation tasks connected to the active journey while excluding unrelated roots.

answers.new_capability: An active headless journey can derive terminal completion evidence, accepted completion, closure progress, and finalization owner from its scoped task graph even when other completed or failed roots exist in the same repository.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Workspace-global completion could pick the latest unrelated completed task, require all repository tasks to be complete, or reject finalization because more than one root task existed.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: CLI Product Completion would remain valid only in isolated repositories and could fail or finalize incorrectly during normal repeated CLI use.
answers.non_duplicative: CLI-C2 is not resume selection, output formatting, installation, or primary run development-path evidence. It changes terminal completion ownership inside the Rust runtime.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The implementation uses existing headless.run.drive, completion acceptance, and finalization paths.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. No report, readiness, digest, history, verdict, summary, or inspection-only surface is added.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Runtime behavior changes by filtering completion closure inputs and finalization owner validation through the active journey root and typed descendants before timestamp ordering.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Long-running autonomous repositories can complete multiple independent CLI journeys without stale historical tasks contaminating terminal closure.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the cli-session-scoped-completion corrective blocker after PR review and merge; cli-real-timeout-resume-evidence remains open for CLI-C3.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: CLI-C2 updates the current phase manifest to describe runtime-owned scoped completion behavior. It does not weaken phase-value, diagnostics, control-plane authority, or product-completion guards.

exit_criteria: Active journey completion scope is derived in the Rust runtime from the journey checkpoint root plus typed task descendants and provenance-linked recovery/retry/continuation tasks.
headless.run.drive terminal completion evidence uses active journey scope before latest-completed timestamp ordering.
headless.run.drive accepted-completion lookup uses active journey scope before latest-completed timestamp ordering.
Completion closure progress uses active journey scope so unrelated roots do not block complete closure.
Completion finalization owner is selected from active journey scope rather than global root_task_ids.
Replay and duplicate-finalization idempotency remain intact.
CLI remains a thin caller and no new runtime RPC or report surface is added.
CLI-C2 closes only cli-session-scoped-completion; cli-real-timeout-resume-evidence remains open.
behavior_evidence: cargo test -p brownie-runtime headless_completion_scope_tasks_isolates_active_journey_root_from_unrelated_roots proves unrelated completed roots are excluded from active journey completion evidence.

cargo test -p brownie-runtime headless_latest_accepted_completion_uses_active_journey_scope_before_timestamp_ordering proves accepted-completion lookup scopes before selecting the latest completed task.

cargo test -p brownie-runtime headless_completion_finalization_uses_active_journey_scope_owner proves finalization owner selection uses active journey scope and replays without duplicate finalization events.
cargo test -p brownie-runtime completion_finalization proves existing global finalization checks still reject stale progress and conflicting owner checkpoints.
cargo test -p brownie-runtime proves existing runtime behavior remains compatible with scoped journey completion.
